Priya M.: quick Q 1 1 flew to nyc with 3 coworkers and we shared an Uber. i paid the whole $62 on my personal card and used the app split but two ppl paid cash to me later. can i expense my share only or the whole ride? what's required for receipts?
Gloria (People Ops): short answer: you can expense the business portion. if all riders were traveling for the same business meeting and there were no personal detours, the company will cover the business portion. you should only claim your portion unless your manager agreed to cover the full fare.
Priya M.: ok. what's the "business portion" look like for a pooled trip? do we split evenly?
Gloria (People Ops): usually split evenly among business travelers present for the same trip segment. if someone had a personal stop or extra miles, reduce their portion accordingly. document the split in the expense notes and show evidence (ride receipt + screenshot of rider list or trip route).
Ken (manager): @Priya M. i'm fine approving your full claim if you ended up fronting for teammates and they reimbursed you in cash and you include proof. otherwise claim your portion.
Priya M.: proof like what? i have the Uber receipt and screenshots showing split confirmations for two riders but one coworker paid me Venmo (screenshot).
Gloria (People Ops): acceptable proofs: 1) the itemized ride receipt (must include ride ID, date/time, pickup & drop addresses, total amount) 2) screenshots showing rider list or split confirmation in the app 3) proof of payment from colleagues (screenshots of Venmo/cash transfer) or signed handwritten note if cash. attach all to the expense and explain who paid what.
TravelTeamBot: tip: for future group trips use the corporate card or request Travel Desk to book a shared car. that avoids personal payment and reconciliation.
FinanceBot: finance requires the original itemized receipt for all transportation claims. if teammates reimbursed you off-app (cash/peer-pay), include evidence of those transfers. for cash, finance needs a signed receipt from the payer with date, amount, and a note indicating what it's for. for foreign currency rides include currency and either a card statement or a conversion note.
Priya M.: if i only claim my portion, is there a calculator we should use?
Gloria (People Ops): not formal, but include the math in the expense note (e.g., $62 / 4 people = $15.50 each; i paid $62, reimbursed $30 via Venmo, claiming $15.50). reviewers will check receipts.
Priya M.: one coworker refuses to reimburse me now. can i still charge the company for their share?
Gloria (People Ops): no, not automatically. if a coworker refuses, talk to your manager. only expenses for legitimate business travel should be charged to the company. escalation to manager + people-ops required; we may approve on a case-by-case basis if manager confirms that person was scheduled to travel for business and refusal was outside normal behavior.
Ken (manager): i back Gloria. Priya DM me the details and i'll confirm. if it was company-required travel, i'll approve covering the unpaid share.
Priya M.: great 1 i'll submit expense with receipts and math and cc you, Ken. thanks! :thumbsup:
Gloria (People Ops): thanks 1 remember: attach the full ride receipt, screenshots of split/rider list, proof of peer payments (if any), and manager note if you're claiming more than your personal share.
